title: How I used AI-assisted iteration to build 31 microgame genres into one Android/HTML5 game
author: GrowDailyFun
selftext:
I’m the developer of THE WHATEVER GAME, a free arcade game where the mechanics change throughout each run instead of staying in one genre. The current build contains 31 microgame genres across nine worlds, boss encounters, daily challenges, unlockable skins, and Google Play Games cloud saves.



AI-assisted coding was used during iteration and debugging, especially while coordinating many small gameplay systems and the Android/web bridge. Generative tools were also used for promotional graphics. I still assembled, tested, rebuilt, signed, and published the releases, and I disclose the AI-generated categories on the [itch.io](http://itch.io) page.



The hardest design problem was keeping controls and difficulty understandable while switching mechanics quickly. The approach that helped was giving each microgame a very small input vocabulary, keeping shared state outside individual modes, and testing the transitions as their own feature rather than treating them as loading screens.



The browser version is free here: [https://uniqapps.itch.io/the-whatever-game](https://uniqapps.itch.io/the-whatever-game)

Android: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.whatevergame.app](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.whatevergame.app)
